rejected.title: The responsibility to protect
card: The responsibility to protect (R2P) is the idea that each state must protect its own people from mass atrocities. These include genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity.
If a state is unwilling or unable to protect its people, the international community should help. This starts with support and peaceful steps such as diplomacy.
If peaceful means fail and the state manifestly fails to protect its people, the international community may act more strongly. Any use of force needs authorisation from the UN Security Council.
R2P shifts the focus from the right of a state to be left alone to the protection of people. It was endorsed by world leaders at the UN in 2005. It is a principle, not a treaty.
rejected.remember: A state must protect its people first. If it fails, the world community should step in.

a.q: According to the responsibility to protect, who holds the first duty to protect a population from mass atrocities?
opts: The state in which the population lives
The UN Security Council
The International Criminal Court
Neighbouring states
a.why: R2P places the first duty on each state to protect its own people. The international community steps in only when the state is unwilling or unable to do so. The Security Council is tempting, but its role comes later, in authorising force.
a.clue: Think about who acts before the world community does.

b.q: In the country of Ardovia, the government is killing a minority group and refuses all offers of help. Under R2P, what is the correct view of the international community's role?
opts: Act with peaceful steps first, and force only if authorised
Send troops at once, as Ardovia has failed its people
Do nothing, as Ardovia's affairs are its own business
Use force alone, without needing Security Council approval
b.why: R2P says the international community should act when a state fails to protect its people, starting with peaceful steps. Any force needs Security Council authorisation. Sending troops at once is tempting, but R2P does not skip peaceful means or the Council.
b.clue: Check the order of steps and who must approve force.

opts: The government of the state where the people live

problems.detail: Why (a) says other countries act 'only' when the state is unwilling or unable. The card says only that they 'should help' in that case. Under R2P, international help to willing states (pillar two) can also come earlier, so 'only' overstates the card.

The right option is the only one with qualifiers ('first', 'only if authorised'). Each of the three wrong options is a flat, absolute course of action, so a test-wise student could pick the hedged option without knowing R2P.

proposal.title: The responsibility to protect
card: The responsibility to protect (R2P) is the idea that each state has the first duty to protect its own people from mass atrocities. These are genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity.
The international community should help states meet this duty. This can include support, diplomacy and other peaceful steps.
If peaceful steps fail and a state clearly fails to protect its people, the international community may take stronger action. Any use of force must be authorised by the UN Security Council.
R2P changes the question from a state's right to be left alone to the protection of people. World leaders accepted it at the UN in 2005. It is a principle, not a treaty.
proposal.remember: The state protects its people first. Others should help, and any force needs Security Council approval.

a.q: Under R2P, who has the first duty to protect a population from mass atrocities?
opts: The government of the state where the people live
The group of states closest to the country
The members of the UN General Assembly
The leaders of the world's largest economies
a.why: R2P puts the first duty on each state to protect its own people. Other countries should help, and may take stronger action if the state clearly fails. Neighbouring states are tempting, but R2P gives them no first duty over another state's population.

b.q: In Ardovia, the government is killing a minority group and refuses all offers of help. Which approach by the international community fits R2P?
opts: Peaceful steps, then force if the Security Council agrees
Peaceful steps, then force without Security Council approval
Troops first, then Security Council approval afterwards
Stay out, unless Ardovia itself asks for outside help
